title: Wedding at Cana, Cleansing the Temple

questions.question: On the third day there was a wedding at what location?
options: Cana in Galilee
Bethlehem of Judea
Nazareth of Galilee
Jerusalem in Judea
questions.explanation: John 2:1 (ESV): "On the third day there was a wedding at Cana in Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there."

questions.question: What ran out at the wedding, prompting the mother of Jesus to speak to Him?
options: Wine
Bread
Water
Oil for the lamps
questions.explanation: John 2:3 (ESV): "When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him, 'They have no wine.'"

questions.question: What did Jesus initially tell the servants to do with the six stone water jars?
options: "Fill the jars with water."
"Empty the remaining dregs onto the ground."
"Bring them to the master of the feast empty."
"Wash the guests' feet with them."
questions.explanation: John 2:7 (ESV): "Jesus said to the servants, 'Fill the jars with water.' And they filled them up to the brim."

questions.question: Where did Jesus go after Cana for a few days with His mother, His brothers, and His disciples?
options: Capernaum
Jericho
Caesarea Philippi
Bethany
questions.explanation: John 2:12 (ESV): "After this he went down to Capernaum, with his mother and his brothers and his disciples, and they stayed there for a few days."

questions.question: What did Jesus use to drive out the money-changers and those selling animals from the temple?
options: A whip of cords
A wooden staff
His bare hands alone entirely
A sword belonging to Peter
questions.explanation: John 2:15 (ESV): "And making a whip of cords, he drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and oxen."

questions.question: Why were the six stone water jars there in the first place?
options: For the Jewish rites of purification
To store drinking water during droughts
To reserve wine from the previous harvest entirely
For the temple taxes given to the priests
questions.correctAnswer: For the Jewish rites of purification
questions.explanation: John 2:6 (ESV): "Now there were six stone water jars there for the Jewish rites of purification, each holding twenty or thirty gallons."

questions.question: What observation did the master of the feast make to the bridegroom after tasting the new wine?
options: "Everyone serves the good wine first... But you have kept the good wine until now."
"This wine is overly watered down and lacks flavor completely."
"Where did you acquire wine from across the sea?"
"You have served too much wine; the guests are sleeping."
questions.correctAnswer: "Everyone serves the good wine first... But you have kept the good wine until now."
questions.explanation: John 2:10 (ESV): "and said to him, 'Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, then the poor wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.'"

questions.question: What instruction did Jesus give to those who sold pigeons in the temple?
options: "Take these things away; do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
"Release them to fly over the city immediately."
"Sell them fairly without deception entirely."
"Sacrifice them instantly for your sins."
questions.correctAnswer: "Take these things away; do not make my Father's house a house of trade."
questions.explanation: John 2:16 (ESV): "And he told those who sold the pigeons, 'Take these things away; do not make my Father's house a house of trade.'"

questions.question: When asked for a sign for doing these things in the temple, what was Jesus' response?
options: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."
"I perform no signs for a wicked generation entirely."
"You shall see the sun turned to darkness immediately."
"My sign is the whip driving sin away perfectly."
questions.correctAnswer: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."
questions.explanation: John 2:19 (ESV): "Jesus answered them, 'Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.'"

questions.question: How long did the Jews say it had taken to build the temple?
options: Forty-six years
Ten years
Seven years
One hundred years
questions.explanation: John 2:20 (ESV): "The Jews then said, 'It has taken forty-six years to build this temple, and will you raise it up in three days?'"

questions.question: How much did each of the six stone water jars at Cana hold?
options: Twenty or thirty gallons
Five or ten gallons
Fifty to sixty gallons
Around one hundred gallons entirely
questions.explanation: John 2:6 (ESV): "Now there were six stone water jars there for the Jewish rites of purification, each holding twenty or thirty gallons."

questions.question: This miracle at Cana was the first of His signs, manifesting His glory. What occurred as a direct result?
options: And his disciples believed in him
The whole town followed him to Jerusalem instantly
The Pharisees sought to trap him for using water purely
He was crowned king of Cana for the miracle
questions.correctAnswer: And his disciples believed in him
questions.explanation: John 2:11 (ESV): "This, the first of his signs, Jesus did at Cana in Galilee, and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him."

questions.question: Which scripture did His disciples remember when Jesus cleansed the temple?
options: "Zeal for your house will consume me."
"My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations."
"The voice of the Lord echoes in the temple courts."
"The righteous shall strike down the wicked in the sanctuary."
questions.correctAnswer: "Zeal for your house will consume me."
questions.explanation: John 2:17 (ESV): "His disciples remembered that it was written, 'Zeal for your house will consume me.'"

questions.question: What temple was Jesus actually speaking of when He promised to raise it up in three days?
options: The temple of his body
The tabernacle of Moses hidden nearby
A new spiritual building in heaven
The coming kingdom of God
questions.explanation: John 2:21 (ESV): "But he was speaking about the temple of his body."

questions.question: Many believed in His name during the Passover feast, but Jesus did not entrust Himself to them. Why?
options: "Because he knew all people and needed no one to bear witness about man, for he himself knew what was in man."
"Because they only sought to make him an earthly king entirely."
"Because they were spies sent by the Sanhedrin secretly."
"Because their faith was built only on the wine of the feast."
questions.correctAnswer: "Because he knew all people and needed no one to bear witness about man, for he himself knew what was in man."
questions.explanation: John 2:24-25 (ESV): "But Jesus on his part did not entrust himself to them, because he knew all people and needed no one to bear witness about man, for he himself knew what was in man."

key_verse_text: His mother said to the servants, "Do whatever he tells you."
